title: Importing a Large SQL Dump Into a DigitalOcean Managed Database
description: DigitalOcean's managed MySQL requires SSL and blocks SUPER. The exact connection string, the flags that matter, and how to load a big dump.
author: SQLSplit

content.text: DigitalOcean Managed Databases don't give you shell access to the server, so you import over the network with the mysql client. Two things differ from a normal import: SSL is mandatory, and you don't have SUPER privilege.
From the database's Connection Details panel, grab the host, port (usually 25060), user (doadmin), password, and download the CA certificate. Then import:

content.title: ERROR 2026 (SSL connection error)
content.text: Managed databases reject non-SSL connections. You must pass --ssl-mode=REQUIRED. If you also get certificate verification errors, point --ssl-ca at the CA certificate you downloaded from the control panel.
Like most managed databases, DigitalOcean doesn't grant SUPER. Dumps that contain DEFINER on views, triggers, or routines will fail with 'access denied; you need SUPER privilege'. Remove them first:

items: Run the import from a Droplet in the same region — network latency to your laptop will make a multi-GB import painfully slow
Watch net_read_timeout — a slow upload over a home connection can trip it; importing from a co-located Droplet avoids this
Split the dump so a dropped connection doesn't waste the whole transfer

content.title: Import from chunks over the network
content.text: Smaller files survive flaky connections and let you resume from the chunk that failed.

faq.question: How do I import a SQL file into a DigitalOcean Managed Database?
faq.answer: Use the mysql client with the connection details from the control panel, and pass --ssl-mode=REQUIRED with --ssl-ca pointing at the downloaded CA certificate: mysql --host=... --port=25060 --user=doadmin -p --ssl-mode=REQUIRED --ssl-ca=ca-certificate.crt defaultdb < dump.sql.

faq.question: Why do I get an SSL connection error importing to DigitalOcean?
faq.answer: Managed databases require SSL. Add --ssl-mode=REQUIRED, and if certificate verification fails, supply the CA certificate with --ssl-ca=ca-certificate.crt downloaded from the database's Connection Details.

faq.question: Why does 'you need SUPER privilege' appear on a DigitalOcean import?
faq.answer: DigitalOcean doesn't grant SUPER, so DEFINER clauses on views/triggers fail. Strip them with sed -E 's/DEFINER=`[^`]+`@`[^`]+`//g' dump.sql before importing.
